title: Validating JVM Compilers via Maximizing Optimization Interactions
problem: Modern JVM compilers perform multiple interdependent optimization phases that can interfere with each other, potentially leading to compiler crashes or unpredictable behavior. Validating correctness across these optimization interactions is challenging and necessary for production compiler reliability.
motivation: JVM compiler bugs from mishandled optimization interactions can cause subtle runtime failures affecting production systems, making systematic validation of these complex interactions essential.
method: MopFuzzer tests JVM compilers using 13 different mutation tools that make targeted changes to trigger specific optimization behaviors. It records profile data—detailed logs of what optimizations the compiler actually performed—and uses this feedback to steer which mutations to test next, focusing on cases where multiple optimizations interact in the same compilation. Correctness is verified through differential testing, comparing results across different compiler versions to catch errors.
key_novelty: Rather than random testing, the approach systematically steers fuzzing toward triggering multiple compiler optimizations that interact with each other in the same run, guided by profile data from actual compilations.
contributions: Introduction of optimization interaction concept for compiler correctness validation
MopFuzzer framework with 13 mutators for triggering optimization behaviors
Profile-guided test generation method to maximize multi-stage optimization interactions
Discovery of 59 bugs in production JVMs (OpenJDK and OpenJ9)

metrics.other: 59 bugs discovered in OpenJDK and OpenJ9
